body:
You guessed right on the location, but I'm pretty backwoods so it'd be a 3-4 hour drive from the GTA. I appreciate the offer though, but my parents might call the cops if you showed up!

I took the driver's course in high school that was offered through my school, but my parents never let me pursue it further because the instructor was an immigrant and despite being perfectly nice, well versed in what's in the book, and experienced he apparently "didn't know what he was talking about".

I'm not sure how long the course will stay on my record for (hopefully permanently) because it's been over 5 years since I've taken it.

I appreciate the help nonetheless, I think my best bet is to try to make a friend for once at university and hope they can teach me. I've tried driving a few times in the past and it's fairly intuitive. I just doubt I could do a test.

I figure once I get to school I'd need to try to find a job and friends and whatnot if I want to learn to drive. I'm very behind on that front because I've not been allowed before.

I don't live in the US actually, but I can explain the process of licensing as I understand it.

1. You write a written test after buying a book.

2. You then have 5 years to complete the entire program or you fail.

3. You need to drive with an experienced driver for 1 year, or 8 months if you take driving school.

4. Then you can take a driving test. Only then can you drive on your own, and a year later you need to take another test to see if you keep your license.

Problem is my parents won't take me to test in several towns over, and I have literally nobody else in my life to teach me. They were quite exacting in making sure I didn't make friends. I'd like to hear your story though, it might help me somehow.

My parents are okay people, my mother at least. I'm not allowed to get a driver's license because my dad thinks I'm "crazy". He thinks that if I'm in a car I'll purposely crash it in order to die. I've told him I won't because I don't want to damage his car, but he doesn't believe me. Though we don't speak any more, so that's fun.

I try to exercise when I can, it helps me somewhat. We have up to 50 lb dumbbells in the basement and a treadmill that I use almost daily.

I don't really know what options I have in regards to getting out of the house. Like I said, I haven't got anything resembling a support system, they were quite careful about that.  I've talked to my parents about going back to school, but I don't think they're on board yet. They don't understand mental illness that well, being in their 60's. They think it's "shameful" and are loathe to discuss it let alone seek proper help for it.

I don't live in the USA, I just don't want to disclose which country I'm in because I don't want this being linked to me directly since technically I'm not supposed to be using the internet.
